{
  "candidate_rtl": "module addr_calcu(\n    input [7:0] address,\n    input [7:0] ptr1, ptr2,\n    input [7:0] b,\n    input control, // control is late arriving\n    output [15:0] count\n);\n\n    parameter [7:0] base = 8'b10000000;\n\n    wire [7:0] selected_pointer;\n    wire [7:0] offset;\n    wire [15:0] addr;\n\n    assign selected_pointer = control ? ptr1 : ptr2;\n    assign offset = base - selected_pointer;\n    assign addr = {8'h00, address} - {8'h00, offset};\n    assign count = addr + {8'h00, b};\n\nendmodule\n",
  "bottleneck": "The measured worst paths start at control and reach count[10:12] with 2.38 ns arrival. The supplied source-localization result identifies a control-dependent mux in the relevant cone, while the mapped paths contain a deep Boolean chain after control enters the arithmetic cone. The evidence is conservative pre-ABC RTL localization rather than exact gate-to-RTL correspondence, so the suspected bottleneck is the late output selection combined with duplicated arithmetic branches, not a proven serial RTL-adder count.",
  "rewrite": "Select the pointer before computing the offset, then compute one 8-bit offset and one shared 16-bit arithmetic path. This removes the two duplicated offset/address/count branches and moves the control mux upstream, allowing synthesis and ABC to optimize a single arithmetic cone. The offset remains explicitly 8 bits, preserving the required intermediate modulo-256 truncation.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Hypothesized positive maximum-arrival improvement, primarily on control-to-count paths, because control no longer selects between two completed arithmetic results. The exact gain is unmeasured and must be established by the required fixed Yosys, ABC, and OpenSTA flow; no timing result is asserted.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Expected to reduce or maintain mapped area by exposing one shared arithmetic cone instead of two branch cones, with possible buffering or upsizing changes due to the earlier control fanout. The candidate must still be checked against the 1311.632960 um^2 cap and all slew/capacitance limits.",
  "functional_boundaries": "The module name, ports, widths, parameter declaration/default, and combinational behavior are preserved. control=1 selects ptr1 and control=0 selects ptr2. selected_pointer is 8 bits, and offset is assigned as an 8-bit subtraction, so offset=(base-selected_pointer) modulo 256. addr performs 16-bit zero-extended subtraction, and count performs the final 16-bit addition; therefore the result is exactly (zero_extended_address-zero_extended_offset+zero_extended_b) modulo 65536 for every unconstrained 0/1 input combination. No clocks, state, assumptions, input restrictions, or don't-cares are introduced."
}
